posts.t: Hi Nego, an FTR is a failure to return to make a new high/low. In you case price did retrace back below your pink level, but it failed to make a new low. It turned at your green level and went on to make a new high.

Hi Nego,

I am seeing great progression here.... Excellent - keep up the good work.

-- 1. You have studied the FTR pattern and understand what an FTR is.

-- 2. You have discovered that FTRs are everywhere you look, on every time frame.

-- 3. You have discovered in back testing that not all FTRs are tradable on return.

-- 4. No doubt you are about to discover that its not just the potential trade from an FTR that is important, it is equally important, if not more important what it means when a FTR breaks / fails.

Every FTR holds some significance, but where they form is important; and understanding the context of bigger picture is critical. Also, never forget IF's golden rule - Only Trade from the Edge. If you keep pushing, you will get there.

As a suggestion, you could try this....

First, read my post here. Its not about the FTR, but applies equally to your study on FTRs.

Then,

-- 1. Read the FTR Marketpedia article again. I read the articles over and over at different times. Sometimes you see something which did not click in a previous read of the article.

-- 2. Read Les_Pauls Journal, specifically when he starts talking about his Sweet FTR.

-- 3. Read Pedini's Jorunal, specifically when he starts talking about the break of an FTR.

-- 4. Read the FTR Marketpedia article again.

--5. Study your charts again.

-- 6. Post back here in the thread what you learnt.

Hello Ezio,

I've marked a couple in the pic you posted. Those probably look like a mess but I was trying to use what you provided - they'll probably be a bit clearer on M1. See also my chart (sorry I accidentally cut off the dates and had to write them in - way past my bedtime!) April 22, 2014 we had a significant high, then on May 9 price hits it and tries to decide what it is going to do: go up or down (the beginning of the blue box.) Price decides to head up so to recap the move: price rallied up to the blue box, then based at the beginning of the blue box, and then rallied up and out of it - that's an RBR and the "B" is your FTR. Price was limited (a la FL, which Harry and If time.

The green lines are what I'd classify as significant highs or lows that price had to figure out before continuing on. If you get time, try marking the FTR's you find when price meets them and tries to decide what to do. Once you have the rough FTR drawn, try dropping to the lower TF's to find more precise limits to your FTR.

Good luck!

This video by rcmacfmay also help anyone investigating FTR's (he calls them FL but as If and Harry and probably others have said, they are really the same thing.) He shows a trade he's taken and how he selected and marked off a level - it's a great resource!

In your example, it is necessary for price to have engulfed demand and for price to have made a lower low before the FTR would be considered valid.
